rules.title: Keep design direct, proportionate, and legible
rules.applicability: All in-scope TypeScript source and tests.
rules.requirement: Code must use the simplest design that preserves its governing invariants. Every abstraction, wrapper, branch, generic, and indirection must own a present responsibility.
rules.rationale: Speculative or pass-through machinery hides intent, enlarges the change surface, and makes locally simple behavior harder to verify.
audit_procedure: Trace each abstraction through its callers, invariants, and present change pressure.
Require a named policy, boundary, lifecycle, substitution, or evidence role for every non-trivial layer.
Report pass-through and speculative structure only when removing it preserves a clearer contract; do not use size or style preference as the finding.

mechanical_enforcement.caveat: A detector or complexity threshold cannot decide whether an abstraction owns real policy.

remediation.guidance: Remove or flatten machinery only after checking callers, exported contracts, error behavior, and lifecycle ownership.

required_evidence: why a simpler shape is insufficient

rules.title: Preserve type evidence
rules.applicability: Assertions, generics, casts, non-null assertions, and boundary adapters.
rules.requirement: Every claimed type must be supported by local static or runtime evidence. Chained assertions, widening through unknown, unjustified non-null assertions, and unconstrained generic escape hatches are prohibited.
rules.rationale: Assertions suppress the compiler without proving the runtime fact. Laundered uncertainty turns type checking into documentation rather than assurance.
audit_procedure: Inventory casts, non-null assertions, assertion functions, and generic defaults or constraints that can erase evidence.
For each claim, identify the local narrowing, parser, invariant, or construction path that proves it.
Report only claims whose evidence is absent or weaker than the asserted type; do not replace useful unknown with any.

mechanical_enforcement.check: repository-owned rules for unnecessary, unsafe, and non-null assertions
mechanical_enforcement.caveat: Lint availability and configuration are repository evidence; source review decides whether the assertion is justified.

remediation.guidance: Replace the assertion with narrowing, validation, a stronger generic constraint, or a construction invariant proven at the use site.

required_evidence: why local proof cannot be expressed

rules.title: Narrow external uncertainty at the boundary
rules.applicability: Network, storage, environment, message, catch, parser, and interoperability boundaries.
rules.requirement: Externally supplied values must enter as unknown or an equally honest boundary type and be validated before domain use. Record checks must distinguish named-field objects from null and arrays when the domain requires a record.
rules.rationale: Static annotations do not validate runtime input. Boundary parsing prevents malformed data and accidental array acceptance from contaminating trusted domain code.
audit_procedure: Inventory external inputs and trace them to the first trusted domain operation.
Verify structural and semantic validation occurs before use and does not rely on an assertion-only parser.
Check object guards reject null and arrays whenever the intended domain shape is a named-field record.

mechanical_enforcement.caveat: Compiler success cannot establish the shape of runtime data.

remediation.guidance: Add the narrowest parser or guard at the owning boundary, preserve useful diagnostics, and keep validated domain types downstream.

rules.title: Make asynchronous ownership and lifecycle explicit
rules.applicability: Promises, tasks, callbacks, streams, timers, subscriptions, and cancellation.
rules.requirement: Asynchronous work must be awaited, returned, deliberately detached with observed failure, or owned by a cancellation and cleanup lifecycle. Shutdown and supersession must not leave unowned work or resources.
rules.rationale: Floating work loses failures, races teardown, and makes observable behavior depend on process timing rather than an explicit owner.
audit_procedure: Trace every spawned promise, timer, subscription, stream, and callback to its owner.
Verify failures are observed and deliberate detachment is visible rather than accidental.
Inspect cancellation, supersession, component or service teardown, and shutdown for cleanup races and stale writes.

mechanical_enforcement.caveat: A lint does not prove cleanup, cancellation, or lifecycle ownership and may be unavailable.

remediation.guidance: Assign one visible owner, preserve rejection paths, and add bounded cleanup without changing product timing or retry policy.

rules.title: Keep failures contextual and observable
rules.applicability: Throws, catches, results, retries, logging, and boundary translation.
rules.requirement: Thrown values must be Error objects or repository-defined typed failures. Caught unknown values must be narrowed, context must be added once at the owning boundary, and discarded failures must belong to explicit bounded control flow.
rules.rationale: String throws, swallowed failures, duplicated logging, and context loss prevent callers and operators from understanding or recovering from faults.
audit_procedure: Trace throw, catch, retry, log, and translation paths across their owning boundary.
Distinguish bounded probes and deliberate fallback from swallowed failures.
Inspect string or arbitrary throws, lost causes, duplicate logging, unbounded retry, and success returned after failure.

mechanical_enforcement.caveat: Lint evidence cannot decide boundary ownership, retry policy, or whether failure context was preserved.

action_overrides.reason: Changing public error shapes, retry policy, status mapping, or user-visible failure behavior changes a caller or product contract.

remediation.guidance: Preserve the public failure contract, retain the original cause, and add context at one owning boundary.

rules.title: Respect package and dependency boundaries
rules.applicability: Imports, exports, package entry points, workspace edges, and dependency injection.
rules.requirement: Dependencies must flow through owned public seams in the repository-defined direction. Deep imports, cycles, leaking internals, and policy placed outside its owning package require explicit architectural justification.
rules.rationale: Visible boundaries keep change impact local. Reaching through internals or reversing dependency direction couples callers to implementation details and makes package contracts unreliable.
audit_procedure: Build a package and import view for the selected audit scope and its direct dependencies.
Compare imports and exports with repository entry points, ownership, and declared dependency direction.
Report deep imports, cycles, leaking internals, or misplaced policy only when the owning architecture makes the violation determinate.

mechanical_enforcement.caveat: Compilation cannot prove the intended architecture and evidence may be unavailable.

action_overrides.reason: Adding or removing public exports, changing package ownership, or reversing dependency direction changes architecture outside bounded repair.

remediation.guidance: Repair imports within an existing owned seam. Stop before inventing a new public API or changing package ownership.

required_evidence: reason the public seam is insufficient

rules.title: Keep reactive computation pure and lifecycle explicit
rules.applicability: Svelte 5 runes code. Older or unresolved Svelte versions make this overlay unavailable rather than changing the rule semantics.
rules.requirement: Derived state must remain pure. Effects must own a real reactive transition or external synchronization, must not hide ordinary data flow, and must clean up every resource they create.
rules.rationale: Effects used as general computation obscure dependencies, create cycles and stale state, and make server and client behavior difficult to reason about.
audit_procedure: Confirm the package resolves supported Svelte 5 semantics before applying the overlay.
Start with compiler reactivity warnings and captured initial values, then classify each effect by reactive purpose.
Inspect effect writes, async tracking, teardown, cycles, stale captures, and server-render assumptions.

mechanical_enforcement.caveat: Compiler success cannot prove that an effect is necessary or that external resources are fully owned.

remediation.guidance: Move pure computation to derived state or direct code; retain effects only for genuine reactive synchronization with bounded teardown.

required_evidence: why derived or direct code is insufficient

rules.title: Treat accessibility as correctness
rules.applicability: Rendered Svelte markup and interactive component behavior under supported Svelte 5 semantics.
rules.requirement: Interactive markup must use appropriate semantics and provide equivalent keyboard, focus, label, and announcement behavior. Accessibility diagnostics and suppressions must be resolved against actual interaction behavior.
rules.rationale: An interaction that cannot be perceived or operated by supported users is incorrect even when its visual happy path works.
audit_procedure: Confirm the package resolves supported Svelte 5 semantics before applying the overlay.
Collect compiler and repository lint accessibility diagnostics and inspect every suppression in scope.
Review semantic element choice, keyboard operation, focus order and restoration, accessible naming, state, and announcements that tools cannot prove.

mechanical_enforcement.caveat: Diagnostics cover known static patterns, not complete keyboard, focus, naming, or announcement behavior.

remediation.guidance: Prefer native semantics and preserve the component's intended interaction while correcting keyboard, focus, name, role, state, or announcement behavior.

rules.title: Isolate request state and server-only data
rules.applicability: SvelteKit 2 routes, hooks, load functions, server modules, and shared libraries. Older or unresolved versions make this overlay unavailable.
rules.requirement: Mutable request state must be isolated per request, load functions must remain free of shared-state side effects, and server-only data must not enter client-reachable import or serialization graphs.
rules.rationale: Shared server state can leak data across users. Client-reachable secrets and server modules break the trust boundary even when tests or development builds appear safe.
audit_procedure: Confirm the package resolves supported SvelteKit 2 semantics before applying the overlay.
Trace module-level mutable state through hooks, loads, actions, endpoints, and request locals.
Trace server-only imports and serialized values into client-reachable graphs, including paths hidden by test-only conditions.

mechanical_enforcement.check: repository-owned SvelteKit build or check diagnostics outside test mode
mechanical_enforcement.caveat: Framework checks do not prove request isolation and startup or routing failure is unavailable evidence, never a pass.

action_overrides.reason: Changing authentication, request ownership, persistence, or public serialized data changes a product or security contract.

remediation.guidance: Move mutable state to request-owned context and keep secrets behind server-only modules without changing authentication or serialization contracts.

rules.title: Record generated-looking indirection without rewrite authority
rules.applicability: Pass-through wrappers, speculative helpers, redundant prose, and abstractions without visibly owned policy.
rules.requirement: Suspected slop must be recorded as a non-failing evaluation signal. It cannot establish a violation, authorize mutation, or substitute for an independently assessed normative rule.
rules.rationale: Generated-looking patterns are useful review prompts but are too contextual and subjective to justify repairs on their own.
audit_procedure: Record every suspected candidate in a separate evaluation ledger with location and observed pattern.
Give each candidate a disposition of retain, corroborated, or not actionable.
Assess corroborated candidates independently under a named normative rule before creating a finding or repair plan.
Never fail the audit, widen scope, or mutate code from this rule alone.

mechanical_enforcement.caveat: The signal is experimental and has no independent finding or repair authority.

remediation.guidance: Do not remediate under TS-SLOP-001. Cite a separate approved rule and its authority or retain the code.

completion_evidence: independent normative assessment for every corroborated candidate
